recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-38861 unless a future work group decision changes the Patient.gender/RSG policy or replaces the Gender Harmony IG linkage.
issue_request: FHIR-38861 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for R5 Patient section 8.1.8. It asked for additional top-level guidance on when Patient.gender versus Recorded Sex or Gender should be used to represent administrative gender, and for correction of the RSG-section typos "clincal" and "an realm-specific".
initial_application: Commit 01c44ce75f41fad6d42eeb5abbfd7c65a23dd4fa changed source/patient/patient-notes.xml and included the exact Jira-requested top-level guidance sentence. Follow-up February 2023 Patient narrative commits including 5529c7d, 988821a, 571ab79, and f57e657 removed duplicated old RSG prose, filled the Gender Harmony links, updated extension hyperlinks, and left the current corrected RSG wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists patient=Patient, so the Patient narrative is in build scope. Patient.gender's StructureDefinition definition links to patient.html#gender. FHIR-39239 confirms Patient.gender should be retained for existing systems, with explicit partner pre-coordination for precise semantics. Confluence Gender Harmony and PA minutes show the RSG/FHIR section text was prepared for the build and then approved through PA block voting; no direct Zulip discussion was found that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/patient/patient-notes.xml already provides the requested use-case selection guidance, distinguishes Patient.gender from RSG, points RSG exchange to the Gender Harmony IG, and has removed the cited typo wording.

related_jiras.note: The same implementation commit and PA block vote updated neighboring Gender Identity text; it was checked as context but is a separate guidance request and was not decided here.
Resolved No Change/Question Answered that Patient.gender remains available rather than being replaced wholesale by Recorded Sex or Gender.
